messages.author: 93b51d5f1096313d
messages.subject: "dyld: Library not loaded" error when trying to run INLA
parts:
My R is version 4.0.3, installed from Conda-Forge. Unfortunately, since I'm not an admin on the machine where I'm trying to run analyses, I can't use the stock R for Mac from CRAN.

I installed INLA with the following R statement:

install.packages("INLA",repos=c(getOption("repos"),INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep=FALSE)

I set "dep" to FALSE in order to avoid installing dependencies that I'd otherwise get from Conda-Forge.

The version of INLA that I have is 21.02.23.

I then tried the test example at https://www.r-inla.org/download-install. When executing the R statement "result = inla(formula, family = "gaussian", data = data)", I got the following error messages:

dyld: Library not loaded: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.0/Resources/lib/libRlapack.dylib
  Referenced from: /Users/jjramsey/.conda/envs/conda_forge/lib/R/library/INLA/bin/mac/64bit/inla
  Reason: image not found
dyld: Library not loaded: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.0/Resources/lib/libRlapack.dylib
  Referenced from: /Users/jjramsey/.conda/envs/conda_forge/lib/R/library/INLA/bin/mac/64bit/inla
  Reason: image not found

I saw from an earlier discussion group message (https://groups.google.com/g/r-inla-discussion-group/c/k70KTQr_M0E/m/0xyEMXKRBQAJ) that executing "inla.setOption(mkl = TRUE)" had helped, and since the "mkl" package is a part of my Conda-Forge installation, I figured that it might help me, too. However, I got the same error message as before.

Is there anything else I could try that might help?

messages.author: 93b51d5f1096313d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] "dyld: Library not loaded" error when trying to run INLA
parts:
I found that another thing that seemed to work was to go to the directory where the "inla" binary is (in my case, "/Users/jjramsey/.conda/envs/conda_forge/lib/R/library/INLA/bin/mac/64bit ") and create symbolic links as follows:

ln -s ~/.conda/envs/conda_forge/lib/libblas.dylib libRblas.dylib
ln -s ~/.conda/envs/conda_forge/lib/liblapack.dylib libRlapack.dylib

Of course, one would need to replace "~/.conda/envs/conda_forge/lib/" with wherever the BLAS and LAPACK libraries have been installed.

install.packages("INLA",repos=c(getOption("repos"),INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep=TRUE)

)

parts:

Helpdesk

On 24 Aug 2021, 11:27 +0200, Thomas F Johnson <t.f.j...@sheffield.ac.uk>, wrote:

Is there a way to specify the version to install? I installed the current version using the following code:
install.packages("INLA",repos=c(getOption("repos"),INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep=TRUE)

I am using RV4.1.1 for apple silicon, and R studio V1.4.1717

I have tried uninstalling and reinstalling both of the above, and there is no other active install of R on the machine.

The error comes about when I run:

install.packages("INLA",repos=c(getOption("repos"),INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep=TRUE)
library(INLA)

N <- 100 # 500, 5000, 25000, 100000
x <- rnorm(N, mean = 6, sd = 2)
y <- rnorm(N, mean = x, sd = 1)
data <- list(x = x, y = y, N = N)

inla(y ~ x,
     family = "gaussian",
     data = data,
     control.predictor = list(link = 1)
)

The error occurs regardless of whether I run the above in terminal or Rstudio. 

Any thoughts?

On Monday, 23 August 2021 at 22:45:54 UTC+1 he...@r-inla.org wrote:
